question: Where CDiplomacyStatus +0x10 (occupation_policy) is written and read, the command and screen that set it, whether an AI chooses one, its messages; and the rest of RebuildProvinceModifierValues read to the end on the listing.

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues
addresses.comment: **A province's modifier, made again from nothing.** 0x49F3E0 to two `ret 4` in one frame, 0x4A0673 and 0x4A0689 (int3 from 0x4A068C), read whole on the listing 2026-10-14 (FINDINGS-occupation.md section A). The database is static_modifiers.txt's, g_static_modifiers ([0x1A86208]); the destination is the CProvinceModifier at +0xFC (values at +0x114), whose +8/+0xC vector is the list of contributors a tooltip reads. In order: (1) 0x4595C0 zeroes the values and empties the contributor vector; the province's list of scaled copies (+0x12C) is emptied (0x4B6260). (2) **Buildings** (+0x310..+0x314) whose level_max (+0x20) is above the fixed-point global at 0x1A870F4: effect (+0x10) = definition->effect_size (+8), then effect = level_current (+0x24) x effect / 1000 (64-bit, truncated), added at the id of the kind at +0x14 (its +0x24); `changed` (+0x28) cleared. **Not put on the contributor list.** (3) `overseas` and the `blockaded` nested in it (RebuildProvinceModifierValues_Overseas). (4) `non_core` (RebuildProvinceModifierValues_NonCore). (5) one of `coastal` / `non_coastal` / `coastal_sea` by the template (_CoastalFamily). (6) `no_adjacent_controlled` (_NoAdjacentControlled). (7) **the occupation policy** (_OccupationPolicy). (8) `blockaded` a second time where the port is blockaded (+0x36C, _BlockadedPort). (9) `land_province` or `sea_zone` (_LandOrSea). (10) `manpower` times the province's manpower (_Manpower). (11) `nationalism` times the province's nationalism (_Nationalism). (12) the province's dated modifiers, +0x13C, the expired ones removed (_EventModifiers). (13) the radar bookkeeping (_Radar). (14) `revolt_risk` times the effective revolt risk (read_static_modifier_revolt_risk; FINDINGS-occupation.md section B). Every static is added whole, id by id over ([0x1A86198]-[0x1A86194])/4 modifier kinds, and pushed onto the contributor vector; the three scaled ones (10, 11, 14) are fresh 0x48-byte CStaticModifier copies (source tag +0x40 = 0xF) scaled by CModifier_ScaleValues and kept on +0x12C until the next rebuild frees them. **Corrected 2026-10-14**: this entry said it ends at 0x4A0673 and folds in 'the province's own modifier list (+0x12C)'; the end is 0x4A068B, +0x12C is the list of scaled copies, and the dated modifiers are +0x13C. FINDINGS-revolt.md section 3's 'eight 0xB94936 / 0x4C0700 pairs - the timed and conditional province modifiers' are inlined vector push_back growth paths (0xB94936 throws length_error 'vector<T> too long', 0x4C0700 is the reserve) and not modifiers at all. Callers include RunMonthlyPass (0x683B9A, every province from index 1, before that month's nationalism decay), RunDailyProvincePass (0x49EE0A, only where the day's repair raised a repairable building a whole level), CChangeOccupationPolicyCommand::Execute, CAddProvinceModifierEffect::Execute, CMapProvince::ChangeOwner and the screen.
addresses.evidence: Every instruction of 0x49F3E0..0x4A068B decoded from the entry and walked branch by branch; each static read is `mov eax,[esp+0x14]; mov eax,[eax+disp]` with disp named by FINDINGS-leadership.md section 7's table. Wrong if a branch target past 0x4A0689 exists (none: both rets are followed by int3 and nothing jumps beyond).
addresses.revises: Comment: extent corrected to 0x4A068B, +0x12C is the scaled copies (the dated modifiers are +0x13C), the whole order written out, the 'eight timed modifiers' reading withdrawn.

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_Buildings
addresses.comment: Each building of the province (+0x310..+0x314, in vector order) whose level_max (+0x20) is above the global at 0x1A870F4 (the fixed-point zero ProvinceGraphics_UpdatePictures compares with too): building->effect (+0x10) = definition (+0x18)->effect_size (+8); `changed` (+0x28) = 0; effect = level_current (+0x24) x effect / 1000 through 0xB99980; province values[building+0x14 -> id (+0x24)] += effect. So a building adds its one modifier kind at its **current** level, fractional levels included, and the building is not listed among the province's contributors.
addresses.evidence: 0x49F46B..0x49F521 on the listing: the `cmp ecx,[0x1a870f4]; jle` gate on +0x20, the imul of +0x24 by +0x10, the push 0x3E8 / call 0xB99980, and `add [edx+ecx*8], eax` with ecx = [[bldg+0x14]+0x24]. No call to 0x86CC20 or inline push_back in the loop. Wrong if +0x14 is not the kind (the only other reading would be a CModifier, whose +0x24 is also its id).

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_CoastalFamily

A missing static skips the step. All three are empty in Their Finest Hour.

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_NoAdjacentControlled
addresses.comment: `no_adjacent_controlled` (static +0x2C) where the province has an owner (+0x330 != 0) and no neighbour shares its controller: with controller_id (+0x338) != 0, each edge of the template (+0x90..+0x94, stride 0x14, neighbour id at +4) whose province is simulated (template +0x13D) and has the same controller sets a flag; the flag set skips the step. A province with no controller, or no edges, and an owner gets it. Empty in Their Finest Hour.
addresses.evidence: 0x49F97B..0x49FBDE on the listing: the flag at [esp+0xF], the 0x66666667 divide by 20 of the edge vector, `cmp [eax+0x338], ecx` per neighbour, `cmp [ebx+0x330],0` before [db+0x2C].

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_OccupationPolicy
addresses.comment: **The occupation policy.** Skipped where owner_id (+0x330) == controller_id (+0x338) or the controller's tag is REB. Otherwise policy = countries[controller_id]->diplomacy (+0xE28)[owner_id]->occupation_policy (+0x10): **the controller's policy toward the owner**, whatever the war - an ally or a country at peace that controls the province applies its policy the same way. Its values are added whole and it is pushed onto the contributor list. The pointer is never null in practice (CDiplomacyStatus::Reset puts the shared `no_occupation` there), so a pair that never set a policy adds `no_occupation`'s nothing and still lists it.
addresses.evidence: 0x49FBE2..0x49FD4A: `cmp ecx,[eax+0x338]` with ecx = [eax+0x330]; the three R/E/B byte compares on +0x334; `mov eax,[edx+eax*4]` with eax = +0x338, then `[eax+0xe28]`, `[eax+ecx*4]` with ecx = +0x330, `mov ebx,[eax+0x10]`, `test ebx,ebx`. Wrong if the status array were indexed by controller and read from the owner, which the register flow excludes.

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_Manpower
addresses.comment: `manpower` (static +0x40) scaled by the province's manpower (+0x320), only where that is above 0: a new 0x48-byte CStaticModifier (vftable 0x15BC568, +0x40 = 0xF), the static's values copied (CModifier_CopyValues) and its name (+0x2C), then CModifier_ScaleValues(copy, manpower) - every value x manpower / 1000, 64-bit, truncated - so **per point of manpower** (manpower 3.000 triples the block). Added, pushed onto the contributor list, and appended to the province's list of copies (+0x12C) for the next rebuild to free. Empty in Their Finest Hour.
addresses.evidence: 0x4A0010..0x4A012E: `mov eax,[ecx+0x320]; test; jle`, [db+0x40], `push 0x48; call new`, 0x45A020, 0x401BD0 with +0x2C, `mov edx,[ecx+0x320]` stored as 0x45A080's factor, the 0x10-byte node appended at [esp+0x1C] = province+0x12C. 0x45A080's arithmetic is the record's CModifier_ScaleValues.

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_Nationalism
addresses.comment: **`nationalism` (static +0x44) scaled by the province's nationalism (+0x24)**, where nationalism is not 0, **the controller holds no core on the province** (the cores list +0x344, id at +4, next at +0xC, against +0x338) and the owner is the controller. The same scaled-copy route as manpower: values x nationalism / 1000. Nationalism is set to YEARS_OF_NATIONALISM (20, so 20000) by CMapProvince::ChangeOwner whenever the old owner was a real country, and loses 83 a month in RunMonthlyPass (after that month's rebuild), floored at 0 - one point a year. Their Finest Hour's block is `local_revolt_risk = 0.3`, so 0.3 x the years left: 5.975 at 19.917. **Nothing here touches the list at +0x13C**; FINDINGS-revolt.md section 3 read the next block as part of this one.
addresses.evidence: 0x4A0130..0x4A0303: `mov edi,[edx+0x24]; cmp edi,ebx; je`, the cores walk comparing [eax+4] with +0x338, `cmp [ecx+0x330],eax` with eax = +0x338, [db+0x44], `mov [eax],edi` as the 0x45A080 factor. Saves: 1 January 1936 has 5 provinces at 19.917, 1 February 19.834, 1 March 19.751, 1 April 19.668 - 83 a month; 52 Chinese provinces appear at 19.917 on 1 April (a change of owner in March).

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_EventModifiers
addresses.comment: **The province's dated modifiers** - the list at +0x13C that add_province_modifier fills (payload: modifier at +8, end date at +0xC). For each node in order: where today (CCurrentGameState +0xBDC) is past the date **and** the date's year, (date - 43800000) / 24 / 365.0 truncated, is above 1, the entry is unlinked and deleted (slot 0 with 1); otherwise its modifier is added whole and pushed onto the contributor list. A date in year 1 or earlier never expires. The country's active_modifiers rule, on a province.

Corrects FINDINGS-revolt.md section 3, which tied this walk to nationalism.

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues_Radar
addresses.comment: Where the province has an owner and values[MODIFIER_RADAR_LEVEL] (+0x180) differs from radar_level_applied (+0x378): old < 1000 and new > 0 -> CCountry::AddRadarProvince(controller, id); else old > 0 and new < 1000 -> CCountry_RemoveRadarProvince(controller, id); then +0x378 = new and -1 pushed onto CCurrentGameState +0xCF8 (CList_PushFront; the hourly intelligence refresh). addresses.name: Province_SetController_InitOccupationPolicy
addresses.comment: **The policy a capture starts with**, in Province_SetController after the old controller has lost the province: where new != old, s = countries[new]->diplomacy[**old controller** id]; where s's policy answers false to slot 14 (only `no_occupation` does), `civil_war` is looked up by name (CNameDataBase::GetByName on g_occupation_policies) and, where it is real (slot 14) and its `allow` (+0x50, slot 6) holds in a scope with country = new and FROM = old, it is stored; where s's policy is still `no_occupation`, the database's entry 1 - the file's first policy, Their Finest Hour's `collaboration_government` - is stored. struct_fields.name: occupation_policy
struct_fields.comment: The occupation policy the array's owner applies to provinces of the other country it controls. **Never null**: CDiplomacyStatus::Reset stores the shared `no_occupation` (g_null_occupation_policy). Written by Province_SetController on a capture (Province_SetController_InitOccupationPolicy - keyed new controller -> old controller: `civil_war` where its allow holds, else the file's first policy, only while it is still no_occupation), by CChangeOccupationPolicyCommand::Execute (the player, from the politics screen), by COccupationChange::Apply (history), by the save loader, and back to no_occupation by Reset (new country, session reset, AnnexCountry for every country's status toward the annexed). Nothing at peace or on a change of hands resets it. Read by RebuildProvinceModifierValues (controller -> owner), the politics screen's rows, and the save writer (written only when slot 14 holds, so a new game's save has none). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: A scan of F's whole-image listing for [R+0x10] stores and loads where R came out of a [X+0xE28] array within ten instructions finds exactly the stores 0x4A2F5B, 0x4A2FBD, 0x550EDA and the reads 0x49FC3E, 0x4A2E8F, 0x4A2F83, 0x6BA296, 0x6BA4E6, 0x6BA6A4, 0x6BA700; the remaining writers take the status in a register (Reset, LoadKey at 0xA482AB, 0x494680). Positive control: every known site was found by the scan.
struct_fields.revises: Type void* -> COccupationPolicy*; the comment now names every writer and the null policy.
